title: Interesting / unique ways you utilized the core scripts for your projects.

posts.author: StandardEnemy
posts.body:
Hello!
I'm currently working on writing a new scene type for my MV project that handles point and click adventure style interactions. It made me think about other interesting ways people have extended or utilized the core scripts to do cool things, like the various 3D rendering integrations across the different engines or all the different contextual menus many plugins create for various things.
Mine isn't anywhere near as cool as those, but I wanna hear about the ways you all have personalized your projects through code!
If you have any examples of awesome things you wrote - be it UI, game mechanics, new scenes, or even an implementation of a programming technique - and are willing to talk about it, please do so!
Thanks

posts.author: RCXGaming
posts.body:
@StandardEnemy
I don't know if you count messing with plugins as modifying "core scripts", but I've done quite a few things and plan to do even more to help customize the feel of my games so they don't look or more importantly play the same as other RM games. I'll put them in spoiler tags for readability:
Spoiler:
#1: Quick Inputs for Menuing
Something that bugged me about other RM games is how stiff they are. Scroll through a list of options to pick Guard for every character, scroll through a long list of items to find the one potion you need, rinse and repeat.
Input fatigue is the number one killer of JRPGs, so I had to do something about that.
I rigged it by overwriting
Window_Selectable.prototype.processCursorMove
so pressing 1-9 on the keyboard on any menu instantly snaps the cursor to their corresponding item.
EX. Blue Salve is item 1 in a list. Pressing 1 will take you instantly to the Blue Salve even if you're at item 15 in the list.
I have a very specific flow in mind for this system, and I think speedrunners will love it because I can see them going: [open main menu] -> [press 1 to go to items & click] -> [press 2 to go to medicine & click] -> [press 6 to go to Miracle Salve item and use it]
Spoiler:
#2: Quick Inputs for Combat
Similar to what I did for general menuing, but specialized for combat instead. I modified Yanfly's Battle Status Window after noticing I could directly rig the inputs there too.
One thing lead to another, and now pressing specific buttons in combat will instantly do certain actions depending on what's pressed, regardless of where the cursor was before. The closest example of what I mean is how Persona 5 or Super Mario RPG handle their inputs.
In order:
* 1 - Attack (Select an enemy with the normal attack)
* 2 - Guard (Skip a turn by defending)
* 3 - Skills (Opens the character's primary Tech menu)
* 4 - Inventory (Opens the combat inventory menu)
* 5 - Character Specific 1 (Quick-utilizes the character's unique skill without having to go into any menu)
* 6 - Character Specific 2 (Quick-utilizes the character's unique skill without having to go into any menu)
* 7 - Delay Action (Voluntarily slows down the highlighted player's speed by cutting it in half. Can be toggled on and off without taking up a turn.)
* 8 - Mid-Battle Equip Change (Allows you to change the highlighted actor's equipment. Once the cooldown is applied, it defaults to Normal Attack selection.)
* R - Analyze (Scans all enemies on the field by showing their weaknesses and status vulnerabilities. Doesn't take a turn and everyone can use it, unless they own a proper Scan ability which shows more.)
Spoiler:
#3: Vertical Yanfly Turn Order
This was a big one for me because I kind of despised the default horizontal version. Now I have it working like this - fastest at the bottom, slowest at the top/off-screen. Getting it vertical was a not-so-simple case of flipping how the X and Y coordinates were being calculated.
But there's some other improvements:
* I added a turn counter (which was inspired by how you did it for At Week's End!)
* The colors of the borders change if a character is charmed (pink for allies, green for enemies which is also green for NPC helpers), yellow for confused, and gray for "can't move at all".
Spoiler:
#4: HUD Upgrades
So due to using Moghunter's HP and HUDs, I couldn't rely on using Yanfly's default functions to show when a character has Absorption Barrier active:
A graphic is overlaid the current HP bar to signify the character is shielded - this applied for both actors and enemies.
Likewise, when a character is under any status that drains their HP, their HP bar turns from red to purple.
On top of each combat menu looking different thanks to modifying Mog's Battle HUD (skills menu has a blue color, the limit gauge menu is green with Burst at the corner, etc.), the inventory itself is upgraded.
These four buttons are categories that open to different item types via a combination of SomeRandomDude's skill extension system and well... making skill versions of existing items so this can work.

One of my weirder rewrites involved disabling the default windowskin and icons and instead directly drawing the window borders manually, and rendering the icon glyphs using an icon font. The main benefit being that I could get a corner radius that wasn't possible with the default windowskin and being able to directly tune HUD elements like gauges and icons based on the window border radius.

posts.author: TobyYasha
posts.body:
I'm currently in the middle of designing a semi-random dungeon generation system(while using Tiled).
Basically, I design the layout first and then add the elements of interest in specific rooms.
This data is then exported in a JSON, which I can then use to determine what maps will be used from the game.
As well as what events may appear in a room.
The events in the room will be further tweaked in another JSON dedicated to generation rules(ex: Guarantee 2 chests out of 4 possible spots).
The system is still work in progress, but I've got most ideas noted down as to how it will work.

Tiled is a game changer when it comes to mapping, at least for me.
It is very flexible and you can easily create maps, while also being able to change the layout, decorations and such in an instant.
You can create lots of layers, group them, duplicate and hide...
Then there's the tilesets, honestly, I've never been a fan of how RPG Maker handles its tileset system.
In Tiled you can use as many tilesets as you want, while not being locked in into a specific spritesheet size limitation.
One thing to be aware of is that you'll lose the ability to automap stuff.
You can bring in back, but it involves setting up yourself(I personally haven't looked too much into it).
Making animations in Tiled is also very flexible in easy.
In the tileset's data(opened in Tiled) you can designate certain tiles as animation containers.
That tile can then be used to construct an animation out of other tiles in the tileset.
And of course, you can also use Tiled as a data layer too(you can even add custom properties to stuff which you can find in the exported JSON).
I personally use Visustella's Tiled plugin to handle the Tiled integration in RPG Maker.
There is also an MV version, although I haven't used that one before.

Nice, I might try something similar with PIXI's Graphics class to replace the nine sliced menu cursor in my project. I wanted to add some interpolated animation to the cursor, but since the nine slicing method they use for the cursor is so heavy by redrawing each segment every time the cursor gets refreshed it impacts performance way more than I think is necessary. I didn't even think to just draw the borders myself with lines. Btw the PIXI shape drawing methods, especially the ones within the Graphics class implement proper pixel lines without anti aliasing via an algorithm I cant remember the name of off the top of my head. Canvas drawing can't natively do pixel perfect lines from what I found so if that ever becomes a problem I would recommend poking around and looking into the shape drawing functions PIXI has.
[EDIT]
Found the name of that algorithm I mentioned: its called the Bresenham Line algorithm. Heres a stack overflow response that has a short summary of what it does and a link to a demo site showcasing it in action if you're curious!
https://stackoverflow.com/a/25279040
